A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same optimizer study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V4 reports original unlearning, quantization, relearning, mode-connectivity and utility experiments on MUSE, WMDP and TOFU, including appendix results.

after.justification: V5 retains these original experiments and additionally reports unequal FO/ZO update-budget ablations and optimizer runtimes.

M1.justification: Both retain the same gradient-compression and AdaZO formulations and the Adam–AdaZO hybrid alternating N-step blocks, starting with FO and ending with ZO. Unequal block lengths are tested as ablations; the proposed procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both cover MUSE-Books/News, WMDP-Bio with MMLU, TOFU forget10, and TruthfulQA, HellaSwag and ARC-Challenge utility evaluation. Quantization and forget/retain-set relearning scenarios are retained. The added analyses use existing coverage.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain their comparator sets, including Sophia, Adam, compressed-gradient optimizers, RS, SAM and ZO where previously evaluated. The runtime study uses existing optimizers, while unequal FO/ZO schedules are ablation variants.

E3.justification: V5 Figure 8 adds controlled comparisons of FO/ZO block lengths 20/20, 10/20 and 20/10 under quantization and Relearn100. Table A2 introduces wall-clock runtime evaluation. Existing benchmark settings and Appendix D training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V5 adds an unequal-budget ablation testing the balance between FO and ZO updates, plus computational-cost analysis. The switch-interval sensitivity experiment already existed in v4 Figure A2 and moves to v5 Figure 7. Existing mode-connectivity and relearning analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or defined uncertainty estimates. V5's additional results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V5 adds schedule and runtime results. Figure 8 reports post-Relearn100 VerbMem of 72.1 for FO=20/ZO=10 versus 32.3 for FO=20/ZO=20. Table A2 reports MUSE-Books GradDiff runtimes of 17.7 minutes for Hybrid and 15.2 for Adam. Existing benchmark tables are retained apart from equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: Section 5 removes v4's erroneous odd-k restriction on the final iterate θ_{kN}, which conflicted with FO-first, ZO-last alternation. This is a limited correction to the mathematical specification. Equations 1–5 and the mode-connectivity definition remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: optimizer downgrading can improve unlearning robustness, and hybrid FO–ZO optimization combines effective unlearning with robustness. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V5 interprets unequal update budgets through the leader–follower rationale, linking excess FO to weaker robustness and excess ZO to weaker unlearning effectiveness. It also explains runtime through avoided backward passes and nested optimization. Appendix A's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the code statement from future release to reported availability. V5 adds per-optimizer runtimes and explicitly names real authors among TOFU model-utility components, while retaining Figure 6's scores. Appendix D's hyperparameter and checkpoint-selection details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V5 adds citations to DeepZero, GRU, Rethinking Unlearning for Large Reasoning Models and DRAGON. These modestly extend the introduction and related work without changing the central research positioning or novelty claim.

P1.justification: V5 adds two introductory paragraphs explaining optimizer grade and the hybrid approach, removes duplicated benchmark discussion, and integrates scheduler discussion into Section 6. There are localized terminology and wording corrections, while the overall section sequence and argument remain stable.

P2.justification: The document adopts ICLR formatting with different typography, text width and extensive figure repositioning. Many plots are redrawn with revised axes, labels and grids. The switch ablation moves into Figure 7, Figure 8 and runtime Table A2 are added, and both detailed benchmark tables are compacted onto the final appendix page.

improvement.justification: The unequal-budget ablation and runtime table add useful support for the hybrid design and clarify computational tradeoffs; the expanded introduction and reported code availability also help. These are limited gains. The new claim of no additional runtime cost overstates Table A2, which shows Hybrid slower than Adam in three of four settings, and the final appendix tables are more crowded.
